deities: Gauri-Shankar (Shiva and Parvati riding Nandi, central later shrine)

history.period: Early 11th century CE; central Gauri-Shankar shrine added 1155 CE
history.summary: The largest of the circular yogini temples, ~125 ft in diameter, on a hilltop above the Narmada at Bhedaghat. Built early in the 11th century CE by Kalachuri king Yuvaraja II (r. c. 975-1025 CE), whose capital Tripuri lay four miles away across the river. A covered walkway rings 81 cells (64 for the yoginis, the rest for other deities including the Saptamatrikas); most images are damaged. The later central Gauri-Shankar shrine (1155 CE) houses the rare image of Shiva and Parvati riding Nandi together. The temple is often claimed to have inspired the design of New Delhi's Parliament House (verify). CSV town 'Jabalpur' corrected: the temple is at Bhedaghat, about 20-25 km from Jabalpur city, reached by a climb of 100-150 steps.

name: Chausath Yogini Temple
town_description: Bhedaghat is a small town on the Narmada in Jabalpur district, Madhya Pradesh, famous for its Marble Rocks gorge, Dhuandhar Falls and boating. The hilltop Chausath Yogini temple makes it one of the district's principal heritage and pilgrimage stops; Madhya Pradesh Tourism operates the Marble Rocks hotel here.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaktism; yogini cult with Shaiva elements)

travel.railway: Bhedaghat railway station - approx 2-3 km (verify); Jabalpur Junction - approx 25 km
travel.road: On the Jabalpur-Bhedaghat road, approx 20-25 km southwest of Jabalpur; well served by taxis, autos and local buses (verify)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the site is best in winter sunlight
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM as a guarded/protected site (verify - timings reported by visitor reviews only)
